- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model underestimates; add 3–7% to forecast to compensate for downward bias.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward spikes in price; apply a 1–3 day lag correction by reducing forecast by 2–5% on next day.
- If 3+ consecutive days of high sentiment, model overreacts; apply mean reversion bias: subtract 1–3% from forecast for next 3–5 days.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast for 5+ days, model exhibits “overconfident” bias; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of true values.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates near end of period; reduce final 3–5 forecast values by 3–7% to match true outcome trend.
